content.text:
I submitted index 17 (Ca 0.327 / Mn 0.673, the composition of the phase CaMn₂O₄). At 1.59 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured.

| Index | Ca fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 17 | 0.327 | 1.59 µA |
| 3 | 0.407 | 0.66 µA |
| 21 | 0.254 | 0 A |

- **Why I started at index 17:** band-gap predictions from MEGNet (an ML model) marked two phases as able to absorb the 3.22 eV light: CaMn₂O₄ at 2.54 eV and Ca₂Mn₃O₈ at 2.69 eV. Every other Ca-Mn phase I checked came out near-metallic or narrow-gap, from 0.15 to 1.5 eV.
- **What the other two measurements showed:** index 3 sits at the Ca₂Mn₃O₈ composition and gave less than half the photocurrent of index 17. Index 21, on the Mn-rich side, gave nothing, which fits the near-metallic predictions there.
- **What remains uncertain:** with only 3 of 28 compositions measured, I can't say where the peak actually is. I bracketed it only roughly, so nearby compositions like index 19 (Ca 0.347) or index 20 (Ca 0.303) could be somewhat better. The Ca-rich half of the library (Ca above 0.41) is also unmeasured. I skipped it because the phases there are predicted near-metallic and photocurrent dropped as Ca went up.
- **XRD didn't help:** I used 2 of 5 XRD scans, on indices 17 and 3. Both patterns were dominated by one peak at Q ≈ 2.78 Å⁻¹, which wasn't enough to identify the phases.
